knowledge.text: In train:0027 and train:0028 the Parents deposited the object into the appliance and cycled its door before the transformation succeeded: in train:0027 the Parent moved apple 1 into the microwave (P8:19), cycled the door (P8:20, P8:21, P8:22, P8:23), took the apple back out (P8:24) and only then heated it (P8:25), ending in 27 steps versus the Candidate's 8; in train:0028 the Parent moved egg 1 into the microwave (P9:7), cycled the door (P9:8, P9:9, P9:10, P9:11), retrieved it (P9:12) and heated it (P9:13), taking 15 steps versus the Candidate's 8. This deposit-and-cycle behavior was not universal across the transform pairs: in train:0022 the Parent opened the fridge once (P3:5) and then cooled the bread it was holding directly (P3:6) before delivering it (P3:8), and in train:0029 the Parent heated the held mug directly (P10:30), taking 32 steps versus the Candidate's 9, though its length came largely from search, since it reached the mug only at P10:27/P10:28 whereas the Candidate took it at Q10:3/Q10:4. Both sides succeeded in train:0022 (8 vs 6), train:0026 (9 vs 8), train:0027 (27 vs 8), train:0028 (15 vs 8) and train:0029 (32 vs 9), and the two remaining transform pairs were Parent step-limit failures that the Candidate completed in 8 steps (train:0021 50 vs 8, train:0023 50 vs 8). Since the Candidate's lower counts in these tasks also reflect shorter searches, the transformation clause's own contribution is not isolated by this batch.
